title: Choux Pastry (Profiteroles)
description: Light, crisp, and ready to cradle cream — the classic French pastry that never goes out of style.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 210°C. Line baking trays with baking paper.
In a medium saucepan, combine water, milk, butter, salt, and sugar. Heat over medium heat until the butter melts and the mixture begins to simmer.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan and forms a smooth ball, about 1–2 minutes.
Transfer dough to a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. Add eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing well after each addition.
After the last egg, increase speed to high and mix for 5–10 minutes until the dough is smooth, glossy, and slightly elastic.
Pipe or spoon small portions approximately 4–5 cm diameter onto the prepared trays, leaving about 5 cm space between each.
Lightly sprinkle cold water on the tray to help create steam and maintain shape during baking.
Bake at 210°C for 10 minutes, then reduce to 165°C and bake for a further 10–15 minutes until puffed and golden. Do not open the oven door during the first 15 minutes of baking.
Remove from oven and pierce the base of each profiterole with a skewer to release steam. Cool completely on a wire rack before filling.

notes.title: No Peeking
notes.content: Do not open the oven door during the first 15 minutes of baking. Choux pastry relies on steam to puff — a sudden drop in temperature will cause them to collapse.

notes.title: Steam Release
notes.content: Piercing the base of each profiterole after baking releases trapped steam and prevents them from going soggy as they cool.

notes.title: Filling Ideas
notes.content: Fill with whipped cream, custard, or ice cream. Drizzle with chocolate ganache for classic profiteroles, or fill savoury with herbed cream cheese.
